items.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.correct: Epidemiology studies the distribution and causes of disease in populations and uses that knowledge to guide prevention and policy.
wrongs: Epidemiology studies individual patients in hospitals only.
Epidemiology is unrelated to public health policy.
Epidemiology focuses only on infectious diseases.
why: The text defines it as the study of health conditions in a defined population.
The text says it shapes policy decisions and evidence-based practice.
The text lists environmental, occupational, and forensic epidemiology among its areas.
items.explanation: The passage defines epidemiology, describes its methods, and explains its role in public health.

items.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.append: Because epidemiology identifies risk factors for disease and targets for preventive healthcare, it most likely ______
items.correct: shapes public health policy.
wrongs: replaces clinical treatment entirely.
studies only genetic causes.
avoids statistical analysis.
why: The text says the field shapes policy decisions by identifying risk factors and prevention targets.
The text says epidemiology has helped develop clinical research methods, not replace treatment.
The text lists many areas beyond genetics.
items.explanation: Identifying risks and prevention targets is exactly what informs policy and practice.

items.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
items.correct: It defines epidemiology, explains its role and methods, and lists its major areas and relied-upon disciplines.
wrongs: It narrates the investigation of one outbreak.
It compares epidemiology with clinical medicine.
It argues that epidemiology cannot prevent disease.
why: No single outbreak is narrated.
Clinical medicine is mentioned only in passing.
The text says the field applies knowledge to prevent diseases.
items.explanation: The passage moves from definition and purpose to areas and methods.

items.prompt: Which quotation from the text most directly supports the claim that epidemiology studies populations?
items.correct: Epidemiology is the study and analysis of the distribution (who, when, and where), patterns and determinants of health and disease conditions in a defined population, and application of this knowledge to prevent diseases.
wrongs: It is a cornerstone of public health, and shapes policy decisions and evidence-based practice.
Major areas of epidemiological study include disease causation, transmission, outbreak investigation, and disease surveillance.
Epidemiologists rely on other scientific disciplines like biology and statistics.
why: This sentence describes the field's role in public health.
This sentence lists areas of study.
This sentence describes relied-upon disciplines.
items.explanation: The correct quotation defines the field's focus on a defined population.

items.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.correct: Sanitation protects health by managing excreta, sewage, and clean water to block disease transmission, especially fecal-oral routes.
wrongs: Sanitation is concerned only with industrial waste.
Sanitation has no effect on disease transmission.
Sanitation systems avoid treating wastewater.
why: The text defines sanitation through clean drinking water and treatment of excreta and sewage.
The text says systems aim to stop disease transmission.
The text says a system includes treatment and disposal or reuse.
items.explanation: The passage defines sanitation, explains its purpose, and describes technologies and the value chain.

items.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.append: Because sanitation aims to stop fecal–oral transmission, improved sanitation systems most likely ______
items.correct: reduce diarrheal disease.
wrongs: increase contact with feces.
have no effect on child health.
eliminate the need for clean water.
why: The text says diarrhea can be reduced through adequate sanitation.
Sanitation prevents human contact with feces.
The text links diarrhea to malnutrition and stunted growth in children.
items.explanation: Blocking fecal-oral transmission reduces diseases spread that way, including diarrhea.

items.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
items.correct: It defines sanitation, explains its health purpose, and describes technologies and the sanitation value chain.
wrongs: It profiles a single sanitation worker.
It compares urban and rural sanitation in a table.
It argues that sanitation is unnecessary.
why: No worker is profiled.
No table appears.
The text presents sanitation as protecting human health.
items.explanation: The passage moves from definition and purpose to systems and reuse.

items.prompt: Which quotation from the text most directly supports the claim that sanitation blocks disease transmission?
items.correct: Sanitation systems aim to protect human health by providing a clean environment that will stop the transmission of disease, especially through the fecal–oral route.
wrongs: Sanitation refers to public health conditions related to clean drinking water and treatment and disposal of human excreta and sewage.
Preventing human contact with feces is part of sanitation, as is hand washing with soap.
A range of sanitation technologies and approaches exists.
why: This sentence defines sanitation.
This sentence describes preventive practices.
This sentence notes varied technologies.
items.explanation: The correct quotation explicitly says sanitation stops disease transmission.

items.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.correct: Antibiotics are substances active against bacteria that kill or inhibit them and are ineffective against viruses and fungi.
wrongs: Antibiotics are effective against all viruses.
Antibiotics are synthetic chemicals only.
Antibiotics have never been used in livestock.
why: The text says antibiotics are not effective against viruses or fungi.
The text says antibiotics such as penicillin are produced naturally, while some antibacterials are synthetic.
The text says antibiotics are used in medicine and sometimes in livestock feed.
items.explanation: The passage defines antibiotics, explains their action, and distinguishes them from other antibacterials.

items.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.append: Because antibiotics are not effective against viruses, a person with a viral infection most likely ______
items.correct: would not benefit from an antibiotic.
wrongs: would be cured by penicillin.
should take antibiotics preventively.
would develop a fungal infection.
why: The text explicitly says antibiotics are not effective against viruses.
Penicillin is an antibiotic, so it would not treat a virus.
The text does not recommend antibiotics for viral illness.
items.explanation: Ineffectiveness against viruses means antibiotics would not help a viral infection.

items.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
items.correct: It defines antibiotics and their action, distinguishes natural from synthetic antibacterials, and notes early historical use.
wrongs: It explains how to prescribe antibiotics.
It compares antibiotics with vaccines.
It argues that antibiotics are always harmful.
why: No prescribing guidance is given.
Vaccines are not mentioned.
The text describes antibiotics as important for fighting bacterial infections.
items.explanation: The passage moves from definition to classification and history.

items.prompt: Which quotation from the text most directly supports the claim that antibiotics target bacteria?
items.correct: An antibiotic is a type of antimicrobial substance which is active against bacteria.
wrongs: Antibiotic medications are widely used in the treatment and prevention of such infections.
A limited number of antibiotics also possess antiprotozoal activity.
Antibiotics are not effective against viruses or fungi.
why: This sentence describes medical use.
This sentence notes a limited additional activity.
This sentence states what antibiotics do not affect.
items.explanation: The correct quotation defines antibiotics as active against bacteria.

items.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.correct: Maternal health concerns women's health during pregnancy, birth, and postpartum, and requires investment to reduce preventable deaths.
wrongs: Maternal health concerns only childbirth itself.
Maternal mortality affects only wealthy countries.
Maternal health requires no family planning.
why: The text covers pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period.
The text says it particularly affects women in low and lower-middle income countries.
The text includes family planning and preconception care.
items.explanation: The passage defines maternal health, describes its scope, and discusses mortality and interventions.

items.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.append: Because the causes of maternal death have highly effective interventions, expanding access to care most likely ______
items.correct: would reduce maternal mortality.
wrongs: would increase maternal deaths.
has no effect on outcomes.
would eliminate the need for prenatal care.
why: Effective interventions for the causes mean treatment can prevent deaths.
The text presents interventions as effective.
The text calls for investment precisely because care can improve outcomes.
items.explanation: If the causes are treatable, better access to treatment would lower deaths.

items.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
items.correct: It defines maternal health, describes its components and disparities, and discusses mortality and interventions.
wrongs: It profiles a single mother's pregnancy.
It compares maternal health in two hospitals.
It argues that maternal health needs no investment.
why: No individual case is profiled.
No hospital comparison is made.
The text says there is a need to invest in women's health.
items.explanation: The passage moves from definition and scope to burden and solutions.

items.prompt: Which quotation from the text most directly supports the claim that maternal deaths are preventable?
items.correct: The causes of these maternal deaths range from severe bleeding to obstructed labour, all of which have highly effective interventions.
wrongs: Maternal health is the health of women during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period.
WHO estimates that about 295,000 maternal deaths occurred in 2017.
Maternal morbidity and mortality particularly affects women of color and women living in low and lower-middle income countries.
why: This sentence defines maternal health.
This sentence gives a mortality estimate.
This sentence describes disparities.
items.explanation: The correct quotation says the causes have highly effective interventions.

items.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.correct: Nutrition is how organisms obtain and use nutrients, and imbalances in essential nutrients cause malnutrition.
wrongs: Nutrition applies only to animals.
Nutrients are needed only for energy.
Too much of a nutrient is always harmless.
why: The text discusses plants, fungi, and animals obtaining nutrients.
The text says nutrients are metabolized to create energy and chemical structures.
The text says too much or too little of an essential nutrient can cause malnutrition.
items.explanation: The passage defines nutrition, explains nutrient acquisition across organisms, and describes malnutrition.

items.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.append: Because too much or too little of an essential nutrient can cause malnutrition, healthful nutrition most likely ______
items.correct: requires balance rather than excess.
wrongs: requires consuming as much as possible.
depends on avoiding all nutrients.
is unrelated to nutrient amounts.
why: Both deficiency and excess cause harm, so balance matters.
Excess can cause malnutrition.
Nutrients are required for energy and structure.
items.explanation: The passage states that both too much and too little cause malnutrition, implying balance.

items.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
items.correct: It defines nutrition, explains how different organisms obtain nutrients, and notes the history of nutritional science.
wrongs: It lists calorie counts for common foods.
It compares human and plant digestion in detail.
It argues that cooking is harmful.
why: No calorie table appears.
Plant and fungal acquisition are described briefly, not compared in detail.
The text says humans developed cooking to advance nutrition.
items.explanation: The passage moves from definition and nutrient types to acquisition and history.

items.prompt: Which quotation from the text most directly supports the claim that nutrition supports life processes?
items.correct: Nutrition is the biochemical and physiological process by which an organism uses food and water to support its life.
wrongs: The intake of these substances provides organisms with nutrients which can be metabolized to create energy and chemical structures.
The type of organism determines what nutrients it needs and how it obtains them.
All forms of life require carbon, energy, and water as well as various other molecules.
why: This sentence describes nutrient metabolism.
This sentence describes variation among organisms.
This sentence lists requirements shared by life.
items.explanation: The correct quotation defines nutrition as the process of using food and water to support life.

items.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.correct: Quitting smoking is difficult because of nicotine addiction but sharply reduces the risk of smoking-related disease.
wrongs: Quitting smoking has no health benefits.
Smoking is a minor cause of preventable death.
Nicotine withdrawal makes quitting easier.
why: The text says cessation significantly reduces the risk of dying from smoking-related diseases.
The text calls smoking the leading cause of preventable death.
The text says withdrawal often makes quitting difficult.
items.explanation: The passage defines cessation, describes smoking's harms and addiction, and explains benefits and strategies.

items.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.append: Because the risk of heart attack decreases by 50% after one year of cessation, quitting most likely ______
items.correct: quickly lowers cardiovascular risk.
wrongs: has no effect until ten years pass.
increases the risk of heart attack.
only helps people who never smoked.
why: A halved risk after one year shows rapid cardiovascular benefit.
The text describes a benefit within one year.
The text says the risk decreases, not increases.
items.explanation: The one-year halving of heart attack risk demonstrates a relatively rapid benefit.

items.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
items.correct: It defines cessation, explains nicotine addiction and smoking's harms, and describes benefits and strategies.
wrongs: It profiles a single former smoker.
It compares smoking with alcohol use.
It argues that cessation programs are ineffective.
why: No individual is profiled.
Alcohol is not discussed.
The text lists multiple effective strategies and benefits.
items.explanation: The passage moves from definition and addiction to health effects and quitting methods.

items.prompt: Which quotation from the text most directly supports the claim that quitting reduces disease risk?
items.correct: Smoking cessation significantly reduces the risk of dying from smoking-related diseases.
wrongs: Smoking cessation is the process of discontinuing tobacco smoking.
Tobacco smoke contains nicotine, which is addictive and can cause dependence.
Smoking is the leading cause of preventable death and a global public health concern.
why: This sentence defines cessation.
This sentence describes nicotine addiction.
This sentence describes smoking's overall harm.
items.explanation: The correct quotation states that cessation reduces mortality risk from smoking-related diseases.

items.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.correct: Health equity means fair health outcomes achieved through need-based allocation of resources, not merely equal access.
wrongs: Health equity means providing identical services to everyone.
Health equity is unrelated to social determinants.
Health equity concerns only genetic factors.
why: The text says resources must be allocated on a need-based principle.
The text distinguishes health equity from formal equal opportunity.
The text ties disparities to wealth, power, and prestige.
items.explanation: The passage defines health equity, explains its determinants, and distinguishes it from equal access.

items.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.append: Because health equity requires need-based allocation rather than merely equal access, providing everyone the same services most likely ______
items.correct: may not eliminate health disparities.
wrongs: guarantees health equity.
increases disparities by definition.
removes the need for resources.
why: Equal services do not account for differing needs and disadvantages.
The text says health equity is distinct from simply equal access.
The text calls for need-based allocation, not that equality worsens disparities.
items.explanation: Uniform services ignore unequal needs, so they may leave disparities intact.

items.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
items.correct: It defines health equity, explains its social determinants, and distinguishes it from equal access.
wrongs: It profiles a single health clinic.
It compares health systems in two countries.
It argues that health is not a human right.
why: No clinic is profiled.
No country comparison is made.
The text calls health a basic human right.
items.explanation: The passage moves from definition to determinants and a key distinction.

items.prompt: Which quotation from the text most directly supports the claim that health equity differs from equal access?
items.correct: Health equity is distinct from formal equal opportunity, such as simply providing every individual with equal access to health care.
wrongs: Health equity is social equity in health.
Disparities in health outcomes can be related to differences in access to social determinants of health.
In order to achieve health equity, resources must be allocated based on an individual need-based principle.
why: This sentence defines health equity.
This sentence describes determinants.
This sentence describes need-based allocation.
items.explanation: The correct quotation explicitly separates health equity from equal access.

items.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.correct: An outbreak is a rise in disease cases above normal expectancy, ranging from local clusters to pandemics.
wrongs: An outbreak is any single case of a disease.
Outbreaks affect only one continent.
Pandemics are smaller than local outbreaks.
why: The text defines an outbreak as cases in excess of normal expectancy.
The text says it may affect a small group or thousands across a continent.
The text describes pandemics as near-global outbreaks.
items.explanation: The passage defines outbreaks, describes their scale, and distinguishes related terms.

items.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.append: Because an outbreak is defined as cases exceeding normal expectancy for a location or season, the same number of cases most likely ______
items.correct: could be an outbreak in one setting but not another.
wrongs: always constitutes a pandemic.
is unrelated to location or season.
cannot be investigated by epidemiologists.
why: Expectancy depends on place and season, so the threshold varies.
A pandemic requires near-global spread.
The definition explicitly refers to location and season.
items.explanation: Since the baseline differs by place and season, the same count may exceed one baseline and not another.

items.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
items.correct: It defines an outbreak, describes its possible scale, and distinguishes outbreaks, epidemics, and pandemics.
wrongs: It narrates the investigation of a single outbreak.
It compares infectious and chronic diseases.
It argues that outbreaks cannot be defined.
why: Investigation steps are mentioned but not narrated.
Chronic diseases are not discussed.
The text provides a clear definition of an outbreak.
items.explanation: The passage moves from definition to scale and terminology.

items.prompt: Which quotation from the text most directly supports the claim that outbreaks vary greatly in scale?
items.correct: It may affect a small and localized group or impact upon thousands of people across an entire continent.
wrongs: In epidemiology, an outbreak is a sudden increase in occurrences of a disease when cases are in excess of normal expectancy.
Outbreaks include many epidemics, which is a term normally only used for infectious diseases.
Pandemics are near-global disease outbreaks when multiple and various countries around the Earth are soon infected.
why: This sentence defines an outbreak.
This sentence discusses epidemics.
This sentence defines a pandemic.
items.explanation: The correct quotation contrasts a small local group with thousands across a continent.

items.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.correct: Water purification removes contaminants using physical, biological, chemical, and radiation methods to make water fit for specific uses.
wrongs: Water purification adds contaminants to water.
Purification uses only chemical methods.
Drinking water standards are never set by governments.
why: The text defines purification as removing undesirable substances.
The text lists filtration, sedimentation, distillation, biological filters, flocculation, chlorination, and UV light.
The text says standards are typically set by governments or international standards.
items.explanation: The passage defines purification, surveys its methods, and explains drinking water standards.

items.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.append: Because a visual inspection cannot determine whether water is of appropriate quality, assessing drinking water most likely ______
items.correct: requires testing against standards.
wrongs: can be done by color alone.
requires no measurement.
depends only on the water's source.
why: Quality standards set concentration limits that must be measured.
The text says visual inspection is insufficient.
Assessment requires checking contaminant concentrations.
items.explanation: If appearance cannot establish quality, testing against standards is needed.

items.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
items.correct: It defines purification, describes its purposes and methods, and explains water quality standards.
wrongs: It narrates the construction of a treatment plant.
It compares bottled and tap water.
It argues that purification is unnecessary.
why: No plant construction is narrated.
Bottled water is not discussed.
The text describes purification's importance for human consumption.
items.explanation: The passage moves from definition and uses to methods and standards.

items.prompt: Which quotation from the text most directly supports the claim that purification removes contaminants?
items.correct: Water purification is the process of removing undesirable chemicals, biological contaminants, suspended solids, and gases from water.
wrongs: The goal is to produce water that is fit for specific purposes.
Most water is purified and disinfected for human consumption.
The methods used include physical processes such as filtration, sedimentation, and distillation.
why: This sentence describes the goal.
This sentence describes the main use.
This sentence lists methods.
items.explanation: The correct quotation lists the categories of contaminants removed.

items.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.correct: Mental health is a broad state of emotional, psychological, and social well-being, not merely the absence of mental illness.
wrongs: Mental health is simply the absence of mental illness.
Mental health concerns only emotional well-being.
Mental health has the same definition in every culture.
why: The text says mental health is not merely the absence of mental illness.
The text includes emotional, psychological, and social well-being.
The text says cultural differences affect how mental health is defined.
items.explanation: The passage defines mental health, describes its components, and notes cultural variation.

items.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.append: Because mental health is not merely the absence of mental illness, a person without a diagnosis most likely ______
items.correct: may still vary in mental well-being.
wrongs: is guaranteed to be mentally healthy.
cannot experience stress.
has no emotional life.
why: Well-being is broader than the absence of disorder.
The text explicitly says mental health is not merely the absence of illness.
The text says mental health determines how one handles stress.
items.explanation: A person can lack a diagnosis yet still differ in overall well-being.

items.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
items.correct: It defines mental health, lists its components, and explains how definitions vary across cultures and theories.
wrongs: It profiles a single patient.
It compares mental and physical health in a table.
It argues that mental health cannot be defined.
why: No patient is profiled.
No table appears.
The text offers a WHO definition and describes varying perspectives.
items.explanation: The passage moves from definition and components to cultural and theoretical variation.

items.prompt: Which quotation from the text most directly supports the claim that mental health is broader than the absence of illness?
items.correct: From the perspectives of positive psychology or holism, mental health is thus not merely the absence of mental illness.
wrongs: Mental health encompasses emotional, psychological, and social well-being, influencing cognition, perception, and behavior.
Mental health plays a crucial role in an individual's daily life when managing stress.
Cultural differences, personal philosophy, subjective assessments, and competing professional theories all affect how one defines mental health.
why: This sentence defines mental health's scope.
This sentence describes its role in daily life.
This sentence describes definitional variation.
items.explanation: The correct quotation explicitly says mental health is not merely the absence of illness.
